title: Synthetic Politics: Prevalence, Spreaders, and Emotional Reception of AI-Generated Political Images on X
screen_reason: The classification is of PROVENANCE, not veracity. Every image in the 2024 US election X dataset was labelled by a single GPT-4o prompt - 'Is this an AI-generated image? Answer in one word: yes or no' - and nothing in the pipeline judges whether an image is false, misleading, inaccurate, unreliable or fact-checked. An image that is wholly truthful (an AI-drawn illustration, an openly playful meme) receives the same label as a fabricated one; the authors themselves note the images 'often exhibit playful, humorous, or creatively exaggerated elements' and repeatedly contrast AIGC with misinformation ('whether superspreaders of AI-generated content display similar characteristics to misinformation superspreaders', 'AIGC sharing appears less skewed [than fake news sharing]', 'its reach, engagement, and influence relative to misinformation'). The 12.33% therefore measures synthetic/inauthentic content, which is not one of the labels the review's CONTENT criterion requires (false, misleading, inaccurate, unreliable, misinformation), and the 10%/80% concentration is concentration of AI-image sharing, not of misinformation sharing. Flagged as a genuine borderline call - see missed_or_uncertain for the fully coded numbers should the review decide that AI-generated content is in scope.
missed_or_uncertain: NOT extracted because the label is 'AI-generated', not 'false/misleading/unreliable'. If the review decides synthetic content IS in scope, these are the rows, already coded: (A) CONTENT, share of items: 'Overall, approximately 12.33% of images related to the 2024 U.S. Election on X are AI-generated according to GPT-4o classification.' value_pct 12.33; denominator = the valid GPT-4o detections among 2,462,132 images processed (approximately 90.5% valid, i.e. ~2.23M images) drawn from a 2.5M-image, 414K-spreader keyword corpus of 2024 US election tweets, 1 July - 30 September 2024; country United States; platform Twitter/X; ground_truth classifier (GPT-4o, validated: F1 0.96 on a 2,400-image benchmark; in-the-wild human validation of 2,000 model-labelled images, Cohen's kappa 0.87, FPR 6.5%, FNR 1.6%); classification_level claim_level (item-level); unit item; sampling_frame keyword_topical; denom_scope topical with denom_selection curated (multi-issue election keyword corpus); topic politics_elections; breadth would be unassignable because no veracity judgment was made. (B) SHARING actor_share: 'among 379,025 users who share at least one image, 23.23% are AI image spreaders' - share of image-sharing users who posted at least one AI-generated image; denominator 379,025 users. (C) CONCENTRATION: 'approximately 10% of image spreaders account for 80% of shared AI-generated images' (Figure 2 CDF) - conc_group_pct 10, conc_share_pct 80, conc_unit user, conc_dimension sharing, conc_group_label 'top 10% of image spreaders'; denom_scope n/a. Also present but not prevalence: 128 AIGC superspreaders = the top 1% by h-index of 12,898 filtered AI image spreaders; 82.8% of superspreaders are X Premium subscribers vs 48.7% of non-superspreaders; of the 88 superspreaders with a clear affiliation, 72.2% are right-leaning (64 right, 24 left, 40 unclear); emotion and toxicity comparisons of comments (16,832 comments on AI image tweets vs 27,848 on non-AI image tweets) are reception measures, not prevalence. The 0.1%/80% fake-news concentration figure quoted in the text is cited from Grinberg et al., not measured here, and is excluded under the 'never keep a figure the paper cites from elsewhere' rule.

rob.design: Keyword-built corpus of 2024 US Presidential Election tweets (existing public dataset), 1 July - 30 September 2024: 2.5M images shared by 414K spreaders; 2,462,132 images submitted to GPT-4o (temperature 0) with a single yes/no AI-generation prompt, ~90.5% returning valid answers. Detector validated twice: on a constructed 2,400-image benchmark (LAION-400M non-AI vs DiffusionDB/DALL-E/Midjourney AI) F1 = 0.96, robust to rotation (0.92) and scaling (0.94); and in the wild on 1,000 model-labelled AI and 1,000 non-AI images double-coded by trained annotators (Cohen's kappa 0.87), giving FPR 6.5% and FNR 1.6%. Superspreaders = top 1% by h-index among 12,898 filtered spreaders (>=5 image tweets, h-index > 0), yielding 128 accounts; partisanship hand-coded by two annotators (kappa 0.91, third-annotator majority vote on disagreements); bot scores from Botometer, obtainable only for accounts created before May 2023 (77.3% of superspreaders, 81.6% of non-superspreaders). No veracity, fact-check or source-reliability coding anywhere in the pipeline.
rob.item6_quote: Is this an AI-generated image? Answer in one word: "yes" or "no".
rob.item10_quote: Overall, approximately 12.33% of images related to the 2024 U.S. Election on X are AI-generated according to GPT-4o classification. In terms of users sharing AIGC, among 379,025 users who share at least one image, 23.23% are AI image spreaders.
